newsitem.title: INDIA: Delhi index down 3.3 pct on political developments.
newsitem.headline: Delhi index down 3.3 pct on political developments.

text.p: Delhi stocks closed down on Monday, following a wave of panic selling in the afternoon session triggered by India's regional Dravida Munnetra Kazhagam (DMK) party's plan to pull out of the ruling United Front coalition government.
The Delhi Stock Exchange's benchmark index ended 29.44 points, or 3.3 percent, lower at 891.56 points.

Traders said reports that DMK had decided to withdraw its ministers from the government but would continue to support the government had reversed the market's outlook. Industry minister Murasoli Maran belongs to the DMK.
"Fears that the DMK decision might destabilise the ruling United Front government fuelled the sudden selling spree," Manoj Choraria of stock brokerage Choraria Investments Pvt Ltd said.
Brokers said that the stocks of multinational and automobile companies were the main losers of a trading day extended by 30 minutes, as speculators and foreign investors sold heavily.
Hindustan Lever Ltd plunged 41 rupees to 1,348.
Bajaj Auto led the overall fall in the prices of automobile stocks. It lost 50.50 rupees to 850.
Hero Honda Motors fell 14 rupees to 605.
